open_points.subject: filesystem file and Portal photo model boundary
open_points.text: The file stays in the folder, and the owner who wants that version renames it, after which it is an ordinary photo.
open_points.question: Are the folder file, the ordinary source photo, and the delivered Portal photo one entity across the workflow or separate models, and who mints each identity from what source?
options: One Photo entity is minted from the filesystem file and retains its identity through delivery.
A source-photo entity is minted from the filesystem entry and a distinct Portal-photo entity is minted by delivery.
The filesystem file is only input data; the Portal mints the sole persistent photo entity when delivery occurs.
open_points.default_guess: Use separate source-photo and Portal-photo entities, with delivery creating the Portal identity.

witness.initial: A Syncthing conflict copy exists beside the selected file and has never been delivered.
events: The owner renames the conflict copy.
The deliverer offers and delivers the renamed file.
The owner reviews the delivered photo in the Portal.
outcomes: The same photo identity spans the folder entry, rename, and Portal delivery.
The rename yields a source-photo identity and delivery creates a different Portal-photo identity.
witness.observer: The owner and any component correlating filesystem files with Portal photos

open_points.subject: Syncthing conflict-copy representation
open_points.text: When one file was changed on two devices, Syncthing keeps the other version as a conflict copy beside it.
open_points.question: Is being a conflict copy a status of a photo entity, a distinct model kind, or merely a classification of an otherwise unmodeled filesystem entry?
options: A Photo entity has a conflict_copy status.
ConflictCopy is a distinct model kind from an ordinary photo.
Conflict copies remain unmodeled filesystem entries that are excluded before photo creation.
open_points.default_guess: Treat conflict copies as unmodeled filesystem entries excluded before an ordinary source-photo model is minted.

witness.initial: A normal file and its Syncthing conflict copy are present in the project folder.
outcomes: Two photo entities exist, one carrying a conflict-copy status or kind.
Only the normal file becomes a photo entity; the conflict copy has no runtime model.
witness.observer: The deliverer and diagnostics that enumerate project photos

open_points.subject: rename effect on photo identity and lifecycle
open_points.text: The file stays in the folder, and the owner who wants that version renames it, after which it is an ordinary photo.
open_points.question: Does renaming preserve an existing entity and change its status, retire one entity and mint another, or cause the previously unmodeled file to be minted as a photo for the first time?
options: The same entity changes from conflict_copy to ordinary and retains its identity.
The conflict-copy entity ends and a new ordinary-photo entity is minted from the renamed entry.
No entity exists while the file is a conflict copy; the rename makes it eligible for first-time minting.
open_points.default_guess: No photo entity exists for the conflict copy; after rename the deliverer mints an ordinary source-photo entity.

witness.initial: A conflict copy has already been observed by the deliverer and left in the folder.
events: The owner renames that file without changing its contents.
The deliverer reads the folder again.
outcomes: The previously observed photo retains its identity and changes status.
A new ordinary photo identity appears after the rename.
witness.observer: The owner viewing history and any deduplication or audit component

open_points.subject: delivery offering and conflict-copy exclusion
open_points.text: The deliverer does not offer such a copy.
open_points.question: What model or status does the offer action read, and is non-offering represented as a persistent lifecycle state, a delivery-candidate decision, or absence from the modeled candidate set?
options: The deliverer reads a Photo status and records that the photo is excluded.
The deliverer creates or evaluates a DeliveryCandidate value whose result is not offered.
Conflict copies never enter the candidate model, so no exclusion state is stored.
open_points.default_guess: Model a transient delivery-candidate decision and do not persist an offered/excluded status on the source photo.

witness.initial: A project folder contains only a Syncthing conflict copy.
events: The calling flow asks the deliverer for photos that can be delivered.
The owner later renames the file and asks again.
outcomes: A persistent photo or candidate exists first as not offered and later changes to offered.
No candidate or photo exists on the first read; an ordinary candidate is created only after rename.
witness.observer: The calling flow and the owner seeing available photos

open_points.subject: renamed conflict copy and hidden Portal state
open_points.text: after which it is an ordinary photo.
open_points.question: Once the renamed file is ordinary and is delivered, does it enter the same hidden Portal lifecycle required for every delivered photo, and on which model is that hidden status held?
options: Delivery creates a distinct Portal photo in hidden status.
The existing photo entity crosses into the Portal while its status changes to hidden.
The renamed-conflict path has a separate visibility lifecycle.
open_points.default_guess: Delivery creates a distinct Portal-photo entity in hidden status, exactly like any other delivered photo.

witness.initial: A conflict copy has been renamed and is now eligible as an ordinary photo.
events: The deliverer delivers it to the Portal.
The owner opens the Portal before choosing to show it.
outcomes: A newly minted Portal photo exists and is hidden.
The source photo itself acquires hidden status while retaining its prior identity.
